_backends_help: Backends are tried in `priority` order; the first that answers wins, so a dead
one degrades to the next instead of going silent. Names are arbitrary — the KIND
is inferred from the shape (webhook_url => agent webhook; url+model => any
OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint), or set `type` explicitly to override.
timeout_ms defaults to 120000 for webhooks and 10000 for LLMs: a hang is
indistinguishable from a crash to someone standing at the box, so keep cloud
timeouts short and let it fail over to local.
NEVER put a real API key here — use token_env to name an environment variable.

cloud_llm.system_prompt: You are a helpful voice assistant. Keep replies to 1-2 short spoken sentences.

local_llm.system_prompt: You are a helpful voice assistant. Keep replies to 1-2 short spoken sentences.

_speech_help: Which engines turn speech into text and text back into speech. Same rule as
backends: dispatch is by TYPE, so a new engine is a config edit, not a code
change. Leave this block out entirely and the legacy top-level `stt` section
below is used instead, exactly as before — no migration needed.
stt: whisper_local  | local whisper.cpp. `model` is a FILE PATH.
WHY IT MATTERS: if BOTH sides are hosted, voice-mcp-server is never started,
so that install needs neither whisper.cpp compiled nor MOSS-TTS set up —
the two genuinely hard steps in docs/client-setup.html disappear. `sox` is
still required either way (it formats audio for the box's speaker).
NEVER put a real API key here — use token_env to name an environment variable.
`url` is optional and defaults to the provider's standard endpoint.
_speech_hosted_example: The no-compile alternative — replace the `speech` block above with this and
export OPENAI_API_KEY. prompt_file still works: it is read and sent as the
bias prompt, so Manglish/menu vocabulary keeps helping accuracy.
_stt_help: LEGACY — superseded by `speech` above, still honored so old configs keep working. Used only when `speech` is absent.
greeting_text: Hi! How can I help you today?
_mcp_token_help: Optional. Set mcp_token_env to the name of an env var holding a bearer token, and /mcp will require 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Leave unset for LAN-only use — off by default.
_fleet_token_help: Shared secret between this server and the boxes, sent as X-Fleet-Token.
Set it to the NAME of an env var (never the secret itself — config.json is
not the place for credentials). When set: box-facing routes (/upload,
the box inventory from unauthenticated callers, and every push to a box
carries it. WITHOUT this, anyone on the same WiFi can repoint a box's
microphone upload URL with a single curl. Separate from mcp_token_env on
purpose: that one authenticates MCP clients, this one authenticates hardware.
Rollout is safe in either order — a box only starts enforcing once it has
been handed the token (trust-on-first-use via the /server adopt push).
_lan_ip_help: Optional override for the address boxes are told to reach this machine on. Auto-detected normally (tailnet/CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10 addresses are always skipped, since boxes can't route to them). Set only if the auto-pick is wrong on a multi-interface machine.
_help_url_help: Where the box's on-screen help QR points when someone taps RST twice. Pushed to every box on adoption, so rehosting the guide never means reflashing. Must be reachable WITHOUT a login — whoever scans it is already stuck, and a sign-in wall is worse than no QR. Empty = boxes use the fallback compiled into firmware.
